newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybean futures end up in slow trade.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybean futures end up in slow trade.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended mostly up in slow trading on Thursday on speculative buying from retail investors, traders said.
The most actively traded Novermber 1997 contract ended at 3,288 yuan ($397) per tonne, losing seven yuan. It opened at 3,300 yuan, hitting an intraday high of 3,301 and a low of 3,282.
July rose one yuan to 3,254, September one to 3,286 and the January 1998 contract five to 3,305.
Combined volume fell to 15,800 tonnes from 21,200.
Soybeans opened mostly lower but moved at high levels for most of the session due to speculative buying from retail investors, traders said.
"Retail investors continued to dominate today's trading with many institutional investors staying on the sidelines due to a lack of market-moving news," one trader said.
"Speculative players are willing to buy under the 3,300-yuan level," he said.
Traders said they expected soybeans to linger around the 3,300-yuan level in the short term.
